output.summary: Evergreen shrub native to the Appalachians of eastern North America, from Alabama to coastal Nova Scotia. It keeps waxy, deep-green leaves for up to eight years and bears showy white, pink or pale-purple flowers, mainly in June. In the southern Appalachians it often dominates the forest understory, forming dense thickets called “laurel slicks” or “laurel hells.”
